intent: The caption inside a SelectTrigger that shows the chosen item's label, or a placeholder while nothing is chosen.
typical_uses: The current choice shown in a Select's trigger

dont_use_when.situation: A fixed caption the trigger shows whatever is chosen, such as a filter chip's name

instead.note: Put the caption straight into the trigger as text.

invariants.text: `placeholder` is shown while the value is empty (null, a value that turns into an empty string, or an empty array under `multiple`) and the root's `items` give no label for a null value; `children` override both the placeholder and the resolved label.
Under `multiple` the chosen items' labels are shown in order, joined by a comma and a space.

anti_patterns.dont: Pass the chosen value as children to show it
anti_patterns.do_instead: Leave children out and give the root `items`; children replace the resolved label, so a raw value passed as children shows the identifier instead of its caption

children.states: children replaces the shown label, as React nodes or a function of the current value that returns them
children.because: `ReactNode | ((value: any) => ReactNode)` - a React node and a function have no JSON Schema representation.

placeholder.states: placeholder is the content shown while nothing is chosen
placeholder.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the value's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the value's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (value, placeholder). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through select.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A placeholder until a region is chosen
A count of chosen tags under multiple
good.code:
<Select multiple value={tags} onValueChange={setTags} items={TAGS}>
  <SelectTrigger aria-label="Tags">
    <SelectValue>{(value) => `${value.length} selected`}</SelectValue>
  </SelectTrigger>
  <SelectContent>
    <SelectItem value="bug">Bug</SelectItem>
    <SelectItem value="feature">Feature</SelectItem>
  </SelectContent>
</Select>

bad.title: The raw value passed as children
bad.why: Children replace the resolved label, so the trigger shows the identifier (eu-central) rather than its caption (Frankfurt).

The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the value's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (value, placeholder). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through select.module.css, not through this.
